title: Where Does the Pattern Occur in the Text?

concept.title: Glue pattern + a separator + text, compute the prefix function, and read off where it reaches the pattern length
body: Find **all positions** where a pattern `p` occurs in a text `t` (occurrences may overlap). For `t = ababa` and `p = aba` the positions are 1 and 3 (counting from 1). Comparing the pattern at every position takes O(|t| * |p|), which is up to 2.5 * 10^9 comparisons for words of 50000 letters.

Make one word `p + "#" + t`, where `#` is a letter that occurs in neither word. Compute its prefix function. A value `pi[i] = |p|` at a position in the text part means that a border of length `|p|` ends here: the last `|p|` letters equal the first `|p|` letters, that is, the pattern. Because of the separator, no border can be longer than `|p|`. If the value is found at the index `i` of the glued word, the occurrence ends at the text index `i - |p| - 1` (0-based) and starts `|p| - 1` earlier.

body.code:
c = p + "#" + t
pi = prefix_function(c)
m = len(p)
positions = []
for i in range(m + 1, len(c)):
    if pi[i] == m:
        positions.append(i - 2 * m + 1)      # the start in t, counted from 1
print(len(positions), *positions)

body: The prefix function is computed in O(|p| + |t|), so the search is linear. The first number printed is the number of occurrences; if there is none, only `0` is printed. This is the original use of the Knuth–Morris–Pratt algorithm: the pattern is processed once, and the text is never scanned backwards.

statement: A text `t` and a pattern `p` are given. Print the number of occurrences of `p` in `t` (overlapping occurrences are counted) followed by the positions where they start, counted from 1, in increasing order. If there are no occurrences, print just 0.
inputFormat: The first line has the text `t`.
The second line has the pattern `p`.
outputFormat: Print the number of occurrences, then their starting positions, all on one line.
constraints: 1 <= length of p <= length of t <= 50000
Both words consist of lowercase English letters.
hints: Build p + "#" + t and its prefix function.
An occurrence ends where the prefix function equals the length of p.
Convert the index in the glued word to the start in the text.

explanation: The prefix function of pattern + "#" + text equals the pattern length exactly where an occurrence ends; the start is computed from the index.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

def prefix_function(s):
    n = len(s)
    pi = [0] * n
    for i in range(1, n):
        k = pi[i - 1]
        while k and s[i] != s[k]:
            k = pi[k - 1]
        if s[i] == s[k]:
            k += 1
        pi[i] = k
    return pi

t = input().strip()
p = input().strip()

c = p + "#" + t
pi = prefix_function(c)
m = len(p)
positions = []
for i in range(m + 1, len(c)):
    if pi[i] == m:
        positions.append(i - 2 * m + 1)
print(len(positions), *positions)
